Meta Platforms Inc. (NASDAQ:META) stock gained more than 2% Tuesday as investors rotated back into mega-cap growth stocks after a recent selloff, even as Meta’s expanding AI funding needs and balance-sheet pressure remain in focus.

The rebound extended to rivals including Microsoft Corp. (NASDAQ:MSFT), while the Nasdaq rose 0.90%, the S&P 500 gained 0.43% and Communication Services advanced about 1%.

Meta is seeking at least $15 billion through a U.S. dollar bond offering, part of a broader fundraising effort expected to reach at least $20 billion. The company is also preparing its first euro-denominated bond sale.

The financing follows Meta’s $25 billion common-stock offering, raised $12.5 billion through preferred shares and its plans to sell as much as $60 billion through an at-the-market equity program, Bloomberg reported on Tuesday.

Meta is using the additional capital to expand AI infrastructure and develop products including Muse Wonder.

Its proposed 30-year bonds were discussed at a yield premium of roughly 2.5 percentage points above Treasuries, about 0.9 percentage points wider than comparable debt Meta sold in April.

Credit Outlook Adds Pressure

S&P Global Ratings lowered the outlook on Meta’s AA- credit rating to negative, citing rising leverage and uncertainty around how long elevated capex and negative free operating cash flow could continue.

S&P expects Meta’s capital spending to reach about $140 billion in 2026 and exceed $225 billion in 2027, while leverage could rise above 1.0 times next year.

Meta disagreed with the assessment. Spokesperson Kamran Mumtaz said the company sees significant product and business opportunities ahead and believes its credit profile remains very strong.

Meta has also disclosed more than $800 billion in future spending commitments, with nearly half tied to leases that have not yet begun, largely for data centers and energy infrastructure.

Experts Remain Cautious On Near-Term Setup

Impax Asset Management CIO for fixed income Ross Pamphilon said investors do not need to rush into Meta’s new bonds, citing weakness in recently issued hyperscaler debt and expectations that technology spending may not peak until 2027 or 2028.

Blue Line Capital founder and president Bill Baruch trimmed Meta to 1.5% of his portfolio from 2.5%, citing elevated capex, negative free cash flow and weak stock follow-through after the Muse launch.

Baruch pointed to expected 2026 capex of $135 billion-$145 billion and estimates approaching $200 billion in 2027 as major headwinds.

Ritholtz Wealth Management CEO Josh Brown also stayed cautious on the intermediate-term setup and removed Meta from his "Best Stocks in the Market" list.

Brown said he would want the stock to reclaim its 50-day moving average near $664 before becoming more constructive.

Analyst Consensus Remains Bullish

Meta carries a Buy consensus rating with an average price forecast of $860.41 across 50 analysts.

Recent actions include Cantor Fitzgerald maintaining Overweight and raising its target to $860, BofA Securities maintaining Buy and lifting its target to $845, and KeyBanc maintaining Overweight with a $905 target.

ETF Exposure

Meta carries sizable weights in the Invesco AI and Next Gen Software ETF (NYSE:IGPT) at 9.26%, Natixis Loomis Sayles Focused Growth ETF (NYSE:LSGR) at 8.82% and Fidelity Disruptive Communications ETF (NASDAQ:FDCF) at 8.78%.

Large inflows or outflows in those funds could translate into corresponding buying or selling of Meta shares.

Price Action

META Stock Price Activity: Meta Platforms shares were up 2.15% at $619.76 at the time of publication on Tuesday, according to Benzinga Pro data.

news.content:
Bitcoin (CRYPTO: BTC) could see a third low this year, according to analyst Benjamin Cowen, who is pointing to the S&P 500 as one of the last major indexes still due for a bigger drop.

Why Cowen Says the S&P 500 Hasn’t Fallen Enough Yet

Cowen said Tuesday that the Nasdaq has already dropped more than 10% this quarter, while the Russell 2000 fell 11% to 12% and the Dow dropped about 7%, closely mirroring 2018’s midterm-year correction. 

The S&P 500 (NYSE:SPY), by contrast, is down only about 4%, which Cowen called a sign it’s "one of the last things to fall" before any policy response from the administration.

Cowen pointed to the S&P’s return path during President Donald Trump’s current term closely tracking his first term, with a correction early in both 2018 and 2026 followed by a similar drop emerging late in both years. 

He said the index has already broken below its 50-day moving average and entered its bull market support band, and expects it to test the 200-day moving average near 7,300 before the correction runs its course.

Why Cowen Sees This Fitting the Midterm Playbook

Cowen pointed to the last three midterm years, 2014, 2018 and 2022, which each produced a correction early in the year followed by a second drop late in the year, and 2026 has followed the same script with a roughly 13% decline already completed earlier this year. 

He argued that widespread predictions the Q4 correction wouldn’t happen simply because everyone expected it mirror similar false comfort around Bitcoin’s own seasonal Q4 weakness.

"We’ve talked about the Q4 dump for Bitcoin and people say, well, it’s not going to happen because everyone’s expecting it," Cowen noted.

"But we said the same thing back in February and the same thing back in the summer for Bitcoin, and every single time it happens anyways," he added.

Why Oil and the Iran War Remain the Bigger Wildcard

Cowen sees WTI crude climbing toward the top of its trading range after the midterms unless a ceasefire holds in Iran.

He said markets have repeatedly priced in an Iran deal this year, only for those expectations to fade within weeks. Over the next 12 to 18 months, he thinks investors could start brushing off similar reports.

Cowen expects stocks to bottom within the next couple of months and then rebound. He sees a potential OpenAI IPO in early 2027 as the next major event for investors.

news.content:
Elon Musk’s SpaceX (NASDAQ:SPCX) could be among the biggest losers from a successful Anthropic IPO, according to a finance professor who says the listing could draw investors away from Musk’s AI businesses.

That’s despite Anthropic reportedly accounting for more than a third of SpaceX’s revenue last quarter.

“The more vulnerable names are listed companies that compete with Anthropic for the same pool of ‘AI growth’ capital,” Cathy Zheng, associate professor of finance at Bryant University, told Benzinga exclusively.

“SpaceX, which now owns xAI and its Grok models, is the clearest example.”

Why SpaceX Could Lose Out

Anthropic’s IPO would give investors a more direct way to bet on advanced AI models than buying SpaceX, which also operates rockets and Starlink.

Anthropic’s Claude competes with Grok, while Claude Code challenges Cursor, the coding company SpaceX acquired in August.

“That creates the possibility of stronger enthusiasm for AI alongside weaker prices for some established AI beneficiaries,” Zheng said.

“I don’t expect the megacaps to be the main casualties,” Zheng said.

Even if Anthropic raises $100 billion, that would amount to less than 1% of the combined market value of Nvidia Corp. (NASDAQ:NVDA), Microsoft Corp. (NASDAQ:MSFT), Amazon.com Inc. (NASDAQ:AMZN) and Alphabet Inc. (NASDAQ:GOOGL), she noted.

“Any rotation into Anthropic is a one-time event, while their earnings power keeps compounding,” Zheng said.

Those companies could also benefit from Anthropic’s infrastructure spending. Nvidia supplies chips, while Microsoft, Amazon and Google sell cloud capacity.

“Money raised in the IPO largely flows back to them,” she said.

Anthropic Is Also SpaceX’s Biggest Customer

SpaceX could benefit from that spending, too.

Anthropic reportedly accounted for 34.5% of SpaceX’s third-quarter revenue, roughly $5 billion. Anthropic’s IPO filing shows computing agreements with SpaceX worth up to $120.5 billion through 2029, although either company can cancel with 90 days’ notice after early 2027.

A successful IPO could help Anthropic meet those commitments, even as its listing threatens to draw investors away from SpaceX.

SpaceX finished its June IPO debut with a market capitalization of approximately $2.1 trillion.

On Polymarket, traders give Anthropic a 28% chance of surpassing SpaceX’s June debut as 2026’s largest IPO by first-day market capitalization, with $7.4 million traded on the market.

For SpaceX shareholders, Anthropic’s success could mean billions in additional business while challenging the premium investors are willing to pay for Musk’s AI ambitions.

news.author: Erica Kollmann
news.content:
A Democratic sweep resulting in a disputed midterm election combined with deeper U.S. military involvement in Iran could erase nearly all of the S&P 500’s gains for 2026, according to Evercore ISI research cited by CNBC.

Evercore released its midterm election analysis Sunday that mapped out several possible election outcomes and the likely market response to each one, giving investors a framework for what could follow once ballots are counted.

How the Worst Case Unfolds

Its bleakest projection begins with a Democratic sweep and a contested result. From there, Evercore sees the S&P 500 sliding more than 10% to 6,800 by year-end if President Donald Trump expands military action in Iran before the new Congress takes office in January. The firm described such a move as "kinetic escalation," CNBC reported.

Timing matters here. The stretch between Election Day and the January swearing-in leaves roughly two months in which political uncertainty at home could collide with conflict abroad.

A drop to 6,800 would cancel out almost all of the index’s roughly 11% advance so far this year. Holders of broad index funds such as the State Street SPDR S&P 500 ETF Trust (NYSE:SPY) and the Vanguard S&P 500 ETF (NYSE:VOO) would see most of a strong year evaporate in its final weeks.

Read Also: Trump Celebrates Republican Victory in Guam — 'Wow, Hopefully an Indication for Things to Come!'

Oil, Credit and Growth Risks

"This would be a ‘dip not to be bought,’" analysts led by Julian Emanuel, Evercore’s chief equity and quantitative strategist, wrote in the report, according to CNBC.

Emanuel pointed to several forces capable of turning an initial decline into a drawn-out sell-off. Among them: a surge in oil prices, widening credit spreads and a slowing economy.

Each would land differently across the market. Higher crude prices typically benefit energy producers such as ExxonMobil Holdings Corp. (NYSE:XOM) and Chevron Corp. (NYSE:CVX).

Airlines, including Delta Air Lines Inc. (NYSE:DAL) and United Airlines Holdings Inc. (NASDAQ:UAL), tend to feel the pain through rising fuel costs.

Wider credit spreads would pressure high-yield debt, a corner of the market tracked by the iShares iBoxx $ High Yield Corporate Bond ETF (NYSE:HYG).

Taken together, the pressures Emanuel outlined could weigh on stocks for months and set up a difficult start to 2027, he cautioned.

See More: Top Growth Stocks

Not the Base Case

Emanuel does not view the scenario as his most likely outcome, but he does count it among the risks he fears most.

His broader advice to investors remains intact. Evercore ISI still recommends buying any weakness tied to the election, as long as the worst-case scenario does not play out. Investors following the firm’s lead would treat election-driven pullbacks in benchmarks such as the Invesco QQQ Trust (NASDAQ:QQQ) as potential entry points.

The Bottom Line

A disputed count alone carries its own set of risks. Escalation in Iran before the new Congress is seated would add another, and Evercore sees that combination potentially pushing stocks sharply lower.

news.author: Chandrima Sanyal
news.content:
The 2026 U.S. midterm elections could create political uncertainty, but JPMorgan sees limited downside for equities regardless of which party controls Congress.

According to a scenario analysis by JPMorgan Market Intelligence, based on Bloomberg prediction market data as of Nov. 1, the S&P 500 could gain between 0.25% and 1.25% across three of the four possible congressional outcomes. Even a Democratic sweep, the most likely outcome, carries a projected reaction ranging from a 0.25% decline to a 0.50% gain.

Read Also: QUICK SPARK: Trump Celebrates Republican Victory in Guam — 'Wow, Hopefully an Indication for Things to Come!'

The analysis assigns a 66% probability to Democrats winning both chambers (Blue Wave), a 26% probability to a Democratic House and Republican Senate (Split Congress), a 7% probability to a Republican sweep (Red Wave) and just 1% to a Republican House and Democratic Senate (The Other Split).

The findings suggest investors may want to focus less on predicting the election winner and more on positioning their portfolios for the potential policy and sector implications.

Five ETFs to Watch

1. State Street SPDR S&P 500 ETF Trust (NYSE:SPY)

The broad-market benchmark is the most direct way to position for JPMorgan’s relatively benign outlook. With projected S&P 500 moves confined to a narrow range, investors may prefer diversified exposure over concentrated political bets.

2. Invesco QQQ Trust (NASDAQ:QQQ)

A Democratic sweep could revive concerns about AI regulation and scrutiny of mega-cap technology companies. JPMorgan, however, argues that legislative restrictions face significant hurdles, making any AI-related pullback a potential buying opportunity for AI bulls. QQQ offers exposure to major technology and AI beneficiaries.

3. State Street Health Care Select Sector SPDR ETF (NYSE:XLV)

Health care could emerge as a beneficiary of a Democratic victory, with policy priorities potentially shifting toward health care affordability and funding. Reuters identifies health care stocks as one of the sectors that could benefit from a strong Democratic showing.

4. iShares Global Clean Energy ETF (NASDAQ:ICLN)

Clean energy stocks could attract renewed attention under a Democratic-controlled Congress. Potential changes to renewable energy incentives and environmental policies could influence the sector’s outlook.

5. iShares U.S. Aerospace & Defense ETF (BATS:ITA)

A Republican sweep could support defense stocks if the administration maintains its spending priorities. Reuters notes that increased defense spending is among the potential implications of continued Republican control.

Read Also: $1 Billion Flows Out of Bitcoin ETFs as Midterm Elections Put Trump's Crypto Agenda to the Test

The election may matter more for sector leadership than for the S&P 500’s overall direction. JPMorgan’s projections suggest that investors should watch policy-sensitive industries while keeping broad-market exposure.

However, these are illustrative ETF examples, not specific fund recommendations from JPMorgan. The actual market reaction will also depend on corporate earnings, interest rates and Treasury yields.

Read Also: Kalshi, Polymarket Put Democrats' Senate Odds At More Than 70%: 5 ETFs That Could Move If They're Wrong

Nvidia Corp. (NASDAQ:NVDA) shares are trading higher Tuesday as chipmakers rebound from a sharp Friday selloff, with cheaper oil and hopes of negotiations with Iran supporting the market.

  • NVIDIA shares are trending higher. Why is NVDA stock trading higher?

Nvidia Stock Climbs as the Chip Selloff Eases

Nvidia shares are higher Tuesday as chipmakers regain ground after a rough few sessions. On Friday, 23 leading chip and equipment makers lost about $1.01 trillion by late morning, and Nvidia suffered the biggest loss in dollars. A 3.6% decline sounds small, but on a company valued near $5 trillion it translated into roughly $185 billion of lost value.

Five companies, Nvidia among them, drove the bulk of the losses. Intel, AMD, TSMC and Broadcom were the others, and the five together accounted for roughly 60% of the group’s losses. Intel started the rout when a disappointing fourth-quarter outlook sent its stock down 28.4%, to $65.92.

The Nasdaq Composite had gained about 0.81% by Tuesday’s mid-morning check, recouping part of Monday’s 1.07% decline, while the S&P 500 rose 0.38%. The Dow, meanwhile, slipped 0.49%. Ten-year Treasuries yielded 4.958%, up on the day, and midterm voting continues with no results yet.

The sector’s rebound could owe something to cheaper oil as investors wait on the outcome. Lower energy prices can ease inflation worries and cut the odds of higher interest rates, which tends to help growth stocks like chipmakers because their value rests on earnings expected years from now. Peace hopes may also lower the risk of supply disruptions.

Cheaper Oil and Iran Talks Give Chips a Lift

Oil’s slide began Monday, when hints from President Donald Trump of progress toward a settlement with Iran sent crude down more than 7%. West Texas Intermediate fell to $96.46 and Brent to $104.77. Tehran sounded receptive as well, with Iran’s president saying the supreme leader had approved broader negotiating powers.

Tuesday’s optimism met a setback. Reuters reported American strikes on Qeshm Island, beside the narrow waterway, and crude crept higher, with U.S. benchmark crude near $97.01 and Brent around $105.22 early on.

Pavel Molchanov of Raymond James cautioned that earlier talks have repeatedly stalled, while Goldman Sachs sees a path to $140 Brent in 2027 should Gulf supply remain depressed.

NVDA Shares Are Rising

NVDA Price Action: Nvidia shares were up 2.45% at $207.02 at the time of publication on Tuesday, according to Benzinga Pro.

news.author: Daragh Thomas
news.content:
Election forecaster Nate Silver says Democrats are clear favorites to take control of the Senate in Tuesday’s midterms, despite needing victories in Republican strongholds that haven’t elected a Democratic senator in decades.

“It would be a really bad night for pollsters if Democrats don’t win the Senate,” Silver said on Bloomberg’s Odd Lots podcast, published Tuesday and recorded Oct. 29.

Silver’s final forecast gives Democrats an 82.4% chance of winning the Senate, up from 57.3% when his model launched in August.

Democrats Lead in Republican Strongholds

Republicans hold 53 Senate seats, against 45 Democrats and two independents who caucus with them. Democrats need four net pickups to take control.

Kansas hasn’t elected a Democratic senator since 1932. Texas hasn’t elected one since 1988.

Yet Silver’s final polling averages show Democrats leading by four points in Kansas and 3.3 points in Texas. Democrats also lead in Ohio and Maine, and in Michigan, where they are defending an open seat.

Silver cited President Donald Trump’s roughly 37% approval rating, economic dissatisfaction and the Iran war as factors hurting Republicans.

Silver said Republicans appear to recognize the danger, citing their polling and campaign activity in traditionally safe states.

“They’re bracing for a landslide,” he said.

Why Silver Trusts the Polls

Pollsters underestimated Trump in three consecutive presidential elections, raising an obvious question: why should anyone trust polls showing Democrats ahead this time?

Silver argues that the problem wasn’t necessarily a systematic Republican polling bias. Instead, Trump attracts voters, particularly younger men, who rarely participate in elections and are difficult for pollsters to reach.

Those voters can be missed or dismissed as unlikely to vote in surveys, only to turn out for Trump on Election Day.

But without Trump on the ballot, many may stay home. Silver points to the 2025 gubernatorial elections in Virginia and New Jersey, where polls actually underestimated Democrats.

He acknowledges that polling errors can still occur across several states simultaneously, potentially changing the Senate outcome. But he argues there’s little reason to assume another Republican polling surprise simply because it happened in previous presidential elections.

Silver said AI could be the one policy area where Congress takes action before 2028, even if the election produces political gridlock.

Silver said he would watch for evidence that voters punish candidates seen as too supportive of AI. Any measures that slow data-center construction could affect demand for chips from Nvidia (NASDAQ:NVDA), a major supplier to the AI industry.

Silver Explains the Polymarket Gap

On Polymarket, traders give Democrats approximately a 78% chance of taking the Senate, slightly below Silver’s forecast.

That’s up from 72% on Friday, when traders were increasingly pricing in Democratic control of Congress.

Silver believes prediction markets have “a slightly Republican leaning clientele.”

He said his model and Polymarket’s state-by-state forecasts had a correlation of 0.995, but suggested large traders could explain some of the difference in their overall Senate predictions.

Silver said calling the Senate a toss-up would be hedging.

“You either have to lie and say it’s a toss up. It’s not.”

After Tuesday’s stock market close, attention now shifts to the polls, which will determine whether Republicans or Democrats control the House of Representatives and the U.S. Senate beginning in January 2027.

Here’s a look at the latest prediction market odds.

Democratic Party Sweep Still Favored

Prediction market Kalshi shows odds of 73% that the Democratic Party will win the Senate majority. These odds are down from 77% earlier this morning, with investors still weighing the potential impact of a Democratic Party sweep.

The odds show the Senate likely being 53 Democrats and 46 Republicans if the races stay as predicted. This would change the current makeup, which is 47 Democrats and 53 Republicans.

Democrats are leading six of the seven key Senate races that are expected to be close throughout the day. This includes Abdul El-Sayed with 75% odds to win over Mike Rogers (25%) in Michigan and James Talarico with 74% odds over Ken Paxton (24%) in Texas.

In Iowa, the race is currently split 50%/50% between Senate candidates Josh Turek and Ashley Hinson.

On prediction market Polymarket, the odds for the Democrats to win the Senate are at 74%, down from 77% earlier today.

For the House of Representatives race, the Democrats have much higher odds of taking control with Kalshi showing 94% odds of the party winning a majority.

The prediction markets currently show the Democratic Party favored to win majority control of both the House and the Senate. This could put the party at odds with President Donald Trump, who has promised to veto anything sent his way.

Polls remain open in many states for several hours with results not expected to come in until later tonight, with some races likely too close to call until all mail-in ballots are also accounted for.

news.author: Chris Katje
news.content:
The 2026 midterm elections will determine which political party will control both the House of Representatives and U.S. Senate. Some members are running for re-election to stay in Congress. Long-time congresswoman and former Speaker of the House Nancy Pelosi (D-Calif.) is among those exiting.

Say Goodbye to Congresswoman Nancy Pelosi

Around a year ago, Pelosi shared she would not seek re-election in the 2026 midterm elections, a decision that will see her leave Congress in January 2027.  

"With a grateful heart, I look forward to my final year of service as your proud representative," Pelosi said in a video, addressing San Franciscans.

Pelosi has been in Congress since 1987 and became the first female Speaker of the House, a role she held from 2007 to 2011 and from 2019 to 2023.

The congresswoman is currently serving in her 20th congressional term and is 86 years old.

Say Goodbye to Nancy Pelosi’s Stock Picks

Along with being known for her years in Congress, Pelosi has become well-known for her stock trading disclosures, which are trades made by her husband Paul Pelosi, a venture capitalist.

The trades are often for significant amounts of money and include trading millions of dollars in stocks and options in some of the most valuable companies.

Stock disclosures have shown millions of dollars in shares bought in some technology names, while other disclosures include an options strategy of buying in-the-money calls that expire in a year or two from the purchase date.

The Pelosis have had success with their trades, but some have also caused potential conflicts of interest and red flags, including buying Nvidia stock ahead of a vote on the CHIPS Act, which was set to benefit semiconductor companies such as Nvidia. Pelosi later reported selling the stock for a loss, a move that turned out to cause the couple to miss out on millions of dollars in potential profits years later.

Pelosi also disclosed buying Tesla Inc (NASDAQ:TSLA) options ahead of pro-electric vehicle orders supported by President Joe Biden.

Disclosures have also shown sales of stock and options ahead of investigations, like the sale of Visa (NYSE:V) shares ahead of a recent Department of Justice probe.

Pelosi has said that she does not share any private information with her husband and that he makes his trades based on his own information and investment style.

Read Also: Where Trump’s Portfolio Meets His Power: Nvidia, Palantir, Dell and More

Pelosi’s Latest Trades

Many investors track Pelosi’s trades, including the Pelosi Tracker on Autopilot, which has over $500 million in assets under management.

Pelosi has disclosed over 200 trades since 2014, totaling more than $225 million, according to data from Quiver Quantitative.

When Pelosi leaves Congress, she will no longer be required to disclose the stock and options trading activity of her husband. This could mean that investors have seen the last trades ever disclosed by the former Speaker of the House.

Trades made in 2026 include:

  • Bloom Energy (NYSE:BE): stocks and options bought
  • Intel Corporation (NASDAQ:INTC): stocks and options bought
  • Uber Technologies (NYSE:UBER): options bought
  • AllianceBerstein Holdings (NYSE:AB) stock bought
  • Amazon.com Inc (NASDAQ:AMZN): calls exercised for stock
  • Alphabet Inc (NASDAQ:GOOGL): calls exercised for stock
  • NVIDIA Corp (NASDAQ:NVDA): calls exercised for stock
  • Tempus AI (NASDAQ:TEM): calls exercised for stock
  • Vistra Corp (NYSE:VST): calls exercised for stock

Pelosi has around two months left in Congress. Without more stock disclosures, these will go down as her last trades.

Major U.S. indices closed mixed on Tuesday, with the Dow Jones Industrial Average falling 0.38% to 51,786.72, while the S&P 500 gained 0.36% to 7,568.92 and the Nasdaq climbed 0.83% to 25,372.01.

Market participants also continued monitoring geopolitical risks, inflation, Federal Reserve policy and upcoming midterm elections.

These are the top stocks that gained the attention of retail traders and investors through the day.

Advanced Micro Devices Inc. (NASDAQ:AMD)

Advanced Micro Devices gained 3.65% to close at $483.90, trading between $473.54 and $497.40; its 52-week range is $188.22 to $658.52. In after-hours trading, the stock rose 5.26% to $509.36.

AMD reported third-quarter revenue of $13.38 billion, up 45% year over year and above the $13.09 billion analyst estimate, while adjusted EPS of $2.09 beat expectations of $1.95, driven by a 97% surge in Data Center revenue to $8.5 billion.

The company forecast fourth-quarter revenue of approximately $17 billion, plus or minus 3%, above Wall Street estimates of $16.23 billion, citing accelerating demand for its Instinct and EPYC products and expanding production of Helios and Venice platforms.

Read Also: 'Marking Their Calendar': Tom Lee Says Investors Don't Have 'Conviction' to Buy the Dip Until After Midterms

Super Micro Computer Inc. (NASDAQ:SMCI)

Super Micro Computer rose 3.12% to $31.39, after reaching $32.28 and falling as low as $30.93; the stock’s 52-week high is $51.40 and low is $19.49. The shares shot up 7.58% to $33.71 in extended trading.

Super Micro Computer reported fiscal first-quarter 2027 revenue of $19.95 billion, up 297% year over year and above the $16.39 billion analyst estimate, while adjusted EPS of $1.81 beat expectations of $1.23, driven by strong demand for AI data center solutions.

The company forecast second-quarter revenue of $19.5 billion-$21.5 billion and adjusted EPS of $1.66-$1.90, both exceeding Wall Street estimates, while raising its full-year revenue outlook to $72 billion-$82 billion.

Arista Networks Inc. (NYSE:ANET)

Arista Networks advanced 3.52% to finish at $169.91, moving from an intraday low of $165.22 to a high of $171.84; its 52-week range runs from $114.52 to $217.41. The shares rallied 9.19% to $185.52 in after-hours trading.

Arista Networks reported third-quarter revenue of $3.66 billion, beating the $3.33 billion analyst estimate, while adjusted EPS of $1.20 topped expectations of $1.08, driven by strong demand across customer segments and accelerating AI infrastructure adoption.

The company forecast fourth-quarter revenue of $3.9 billion-$4 billion and adjusted EPS of $1.26-$1.30, both exceeding Wall Street estimates.

Astera Labs Inc. (NASDAQ:ALAB)

Astera Labs climbed 1.72% to close at $233.62, despite fluctuating between $231 and $249.50; the stock’s 52-week high is $499.48 and low is $97.89. The shares fell 2.81% to $227.06 in extended trading.

Astera Labs reported third-quarter revenue of $584.90 million, up 154% year over year and above the $550.80 million analyst estimate, while adjusted EPS of $1.32 beat expectations of $1.19, driven by strong demand for its Scorpio connectivity products.

The company forecast fourth-quarter revenue of $730 million-$750 million and adjusted EPS of $1.62-$1.66, both exceeding Wall Street estimates, although shares fell 6.16% in after-hours trading.

Nvidia Corp. (NASDAQ:NVDA)

Nvidia gained 2.29% to end at $206.69, trading between $205.93 and $209.14; its 52-week range is $164.27 to $243.37.

The chipmaker reportedly asked worldwide data-center partners to restrict sales of cloud-computing services to Chinese customers, requiring at least 51% of service revenue to come from non-Chinese customers.

Benzinga Edge rankings indicate AMD stock has a Momentum score in the 95th percentile and a Value score in the 4th percentile.

news.content:
Cardone Capital founder and entrepreneur Grant Cardone warned on Tuesday that James Talarico‘s Texas Senate race win over GOP’s Ken Paxton could pose challenges to Space Exploration Technologies Corp. (NASDAQ:SPCX) as Democrats secure key victories in the midterm elections.

Trouble For Elon Musk?

In a post on X, Cardone expressed concern over the Senate elections in Texas between Talarico and former Attorney General Paxton. “If talarico wins Texas it won’t be good for SpaceX or the AI bet 🤖,” he said in the post.

Read Also: QUICK SPARK: Elon Musk Says 'Vote Red' — SpaceX And Tesla Have Plenty at Stake

Notably, according to Talarico’s official campaign website, the Texas Democrat has outlined that AI data centers would need to fund their own infrastructure needs, reduce pollution and water consumption.

Talarico has also called for establishing federal standards to protect the power grid and the environment, as well as calling for kicking off an AI dividend.

He said that the dividend would “institute a tax on the AI-attributable profits and use that tax to issue annual dividends to Americans and pay for entrepreneurship grants.” AP News called Talarico the winner of the Senate race in Texas, beating Paxton on Tuesday.

James Talarico Vs. Elon Musk

Musk has delivered sharp criticism of Talarico several times in the run-up to the Texas Senate race, calling the latter a “far left extremist” on one occasion. Talarico, on the other hand, has also voiced his criticism of the Tesla Inc. (NASDAQ:TSLA) CEO, saying that his businesses have been successful due to taxpayer dollars.

Notably, both SpaceX and Tesla are headquartered in Texas, with the commercial spaceflight company establishing the town of Starbase, Texas, which was officially incorporated as a city in May, 2025. SpaceX is also establishing another Starbase in Louisiana.

Musk has also backed Paxton in the Senate race, with the billionaire reportedly donating close to $158 million to political action groups aligned with Paxton in the run-up to the midterm elections.

Gina Hinojosa’s Data Center Moratorium

Besides Talarico, Democratic gubernatorial nominee Gina Hinojosa, who won the Texas gubernatorial race on Tuesday according to AP News, has been a vocal advocate of an AI data center moratorium.

Investor Brad Gerstner, speaking on the Fireside Podcast on Tuesday, warned that a win for Hinojosa could spark challenges to data center buildouts.

“The big fear is that in a blue tsunami, particularly in the state of Texas, you have Hinojosa, who will issue a moratorium on new data centers, may make it difficult for the existing data centers to get permitted,” he said. Gerstner also called the fears overblown.

He also said that AI stocks recorded about a “5 to 10% reversal in the last two hours on the news” in overseas trading in countries like Japan and South Korea.

Notably, NVIDIA Corp (NASDAQ:NVDA) shares were down 2.38% in overnight trading to $201.78, while SPCX shares were down 6.69% to $131.85. CoreWeave Inc. (NASDAQ:CRWV) shares were down 7.35% to $49.79. TSLA shares were down 5.23% to $377.65.
